chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from al-Nawfali from al-Sakuni from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That Ali (peace be upon him) was asked about a fish whose belly was slit and another fish was found inside it, he said: 'Eat both of them together.'
ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to eat a fish that contains another fish inside it according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* within the chapter on hunting and slaughter, this narration from Imam Ali (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of consuming nested fish, reflecting the Shia juristic view that the inner fish is considered part of the outer one’s flesh. This ruling underscores the principle of *istihlak* (subsumption) in marine life, where the presence of one creature within another does not render the outer one impure or inedible, provided the outer fish is caught properly.
